title: Caption a picture
summary: Type a caption right under a picture, so you remember why you saved it.
benefit: A board full of pictures still makes sense when you come back to it weeks later.
outcome: Your picture has a caption underneath it that travels with it around the board and turns up in Fetch.
prerequisites: A picture on a board you can edit.

sections.title: Keep the note with the picture
paragraphs: A caption sits under the picture, on the same card. Move or resize the picture and the caption comes with it.
For example, caption a photo of a harbour café with Harbour café: water bowls outside, dogs welcome on the terrace, then drop it next to your other ideas for the weekend.

flow.entry: Find the picture on your board.

steps.action: Double-click the picture. On a touch screen, tap it once to select it, then double-tap it.
steps.result: A text box opens under the picture, saying “Add a caption…”.

steps.action: Type the caption. Press Enter to start a new line if you want more than one.
steps.result: The text appears under the picture as you type, in the same size it will have on the card.

steps.action: Press Escape, press ⌘Enter (Ctrl+Enter on Windows), or click anywhere else on the board.
steps.result: The caption is saved under the picture.

flow.completion: The caption saves as you type and syncs to everyone on the board. It stays with the picture when you move it, copy it or reopen the board.
flow.correction: Double-click the picture again to change the caption. Delete all the text to remove it. Undo after you finish puts the caption back how it was.

figures.alt: Two photos side by side. The first, a beach at sunset, is captioned Dog-friendly beach north of the pier. The second, a harbour with sailing boats, is selected and its caption reads Harbour café: water bowls outside, dogs welcome on the terrace.
figures.caption: Typing a caption under the harbour photo. The beach photo already has one.

sections.title: Find pictures by their captions
paragraphs: Fetch searches captions, so typing café finds the harbour photo on any board you can open. The caption is also what screen readers announce for the picture.
People with view-only access, including anyone with a share link, see captions but can't change them. Export PNG in the board's … menu includes captions in the picture.
